payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Given the inventory and nested boundary map, does independent inspection establish completed stuffing, affirmative incompleteness, or unresolved completion, and what requested progress is actually established?
node.criteria: Pass only when established paper-and-cup identity and concrete entry, containment, or compression establish completed stuffing; some paper may remain outside. Fail when affirmative geometry establishes incomplete insertion, wholly external placement, rim-only placement without stuffing, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether this failure accompanies positive requested insertion progress or established no progress. Unknown when completion requires an unresolved spatial relation or receiver identity, or when established entry cannot be distinguished as intermediate versus completed stuffing. A boundary-mapping pass is not positive entry evidence. Unresolved source correspondence alone does not invalidate established spatial evidence, but an unresolved edited receiver identity prevents claiming insertion into a cup.
node.binding: Consume s1 and s4_opening_entry in saved order as context, then inspect the edited image independently. Read the nested check's typed identity, geometry, progress, and completion findings rather than treating its execution status as their truth value. Revisit specifically localized hidden paper segments and test whether visible containment, compression, or boundary continuity settles stuffing extent. Resolve conflicts only with explicit visible evidence. Do not promote a mapping pass to entry, an entry finding to completion, or completion failure to no progress. Preserve genuine hidden-entry uncertainty; do not infer missing visual facts from the instruction, source cup, hand grip, or altered printing.
